title: Make a Square with the Same Color
statement:
`grid` is a 3 by 3 board whose cells are painted either black (`'B'`) or white (`'W'`). You may repaint at most one cell to the other color (or repaint nothing).

Return `true` if you can choose the repaint (or none) so that some 2 by 2 block of adjacent cells ends up with all four cells in one color, and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

A 2 by 2 block can be made one color with at most one repaint exactly when at most one of its four cells disagrees with the rest, that is, when it holds 0, 1, 3 or 4 black cells. The only hopeless block is a 2–2 split, because fixing it needs two repaints. A 3 by 3 board has just four 2 by 2 blocks, so checking each one directly is the whole solution. Trying all ten "repaint nothing or one cell" options and scanning the board each time also works, but it is the same idea done the long way.

## Approach

1. Visit the top-left corner (`row`, `col`) of each 2 by 2 block, with both in `0..1`.
2. Count the `black` cells in that block using the four offsets `(dr, dc)`.
3. If `black` is not `2`, this block is already uniform or one repaint away, so return `true`.
4. If all four blocks are 2–2 splits, return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`grid = [["B","W","B"],["B","W","W"],["B","W","B"]]`. The block at `row = 0, col = 0` holds `B, W, B, W`, so `black = 2`: no luck. The block at `row = 0, col = 1` holds `W, B, W, W`, so `black = 1`. Repainting its one black cell, `grid[0][2]`, makes it all white, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): four blocks of four cells each.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Count both colors implicitly: `black = 0` (all white) is a success too, not only `black = 4`.
- The corner loops stop before `2`, not `3`: a block whose corner sits in the last row or column would run off the board.
- Zero repaints is allowed, so a block that is already uniform counts.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `row`, `col` | top-left corner of the current 2 by 2 block |
| `dr`, `dc` | offset of one cell inside the block |
| `black` | number of `'B'` cells in the block |

narration.2: Try every top-left row of a 2 by 2 block: 0 or 1.
narration.3: Try every top-left column of a 2 by 2 block: 0 or 1.
narration.4: Start counting black cells in this block.
narration.5: Visit the four cells of the block by their offsets.
narration.8: Any split other than two and two needs at most one repaint, so the block can be made one color.
narration.11: Every block is split two and two, so one repaint is never enough.
